steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish with cooking spray.
Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir onion in hot oil until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add ground beef and basil. Cook and stir until beef is crumbly and browned, about 5 minutes.
Mix in green beans, tomatoes, and garlic; cook until beans are slightly softened, about 5 minutes more.
Transfer to the prepared casserole dish.
Mix together mashed potatoes, water, and beaten egg in a medium bowl until smooth. Spread evenly over beef mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until potatoes start to brown on top, 15 to 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with cheese and continue baking until cheese is melted, about 5 more minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Ground Beef Shepherd's Pie
raw_recipe.description: This shepherd's pie with ground beef is packed with fresh vegetables for a baked casserole topped with creamy mashed potatoes and Cheddar cheese.
raw_recipe.name: Ground Beef Shepherd's Pie

review.reviewBody: I think Ginger P. has given us a terrific basic recipe that you can change to suit your own tastes! My husband and I really like bold flavors, so here are my modifications. I seasoned the meat heavily by adding garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper, basil, and a small pinch of red pepper. I too, added 1 bag of frozen mixed veggies, thawed in the microwave. Once I had my meat mixture, onion, spices, and veggies combined, I added 1 can of cream of mushroom soup. Also, I doubled the potatoes. I mashed them with 1 small can of evaporated milk, and 1/2 stick of butter, 1 egg, salt, pepper, and some garlic powder. Oh and every chance I get now, I substitute ground CHICKEN for ground beef! I saw it earlier this year at the grocery and decided to try it. It is SO good, and not at all like the flavor of ground turkey which can be very stong. This dish turned out SO good and was very flavorful! Play around with it and have fun :-)

Very good ! I doubled the meat, potatoes and egg . I chose mushrooms, celery and carrots sautéed separately ( adding the carrots for the last minute or two) & layers it on top of the meat . I used the potato water in the potato/egg mashup . Also added Worcestershire and marinara sauce to the meat & onion while frying it up . Delicious and a big hit

I agree that this was easy to put together. I cooked lean ground beef with onion and garlic and basil. After it was cooked, I added a can of petite, diced tomatoes and a 12 ounce bag of frozen mixed vegetables. I purchased Bob Evans 12 ounce mashed potatoes and cooked them in the microwave for 5 minutes. After the beef mixture was heated through, I mixed the cooked potatoes with the water and egg. I put the beef mixture in the casserole dish and covered it with the potato/egg mixture. I cooked it for 25 minutes at 350, added 1/2 cup of shredded sharp cheddar and cooked for another 5 minutes. This was good, but next time I would add more spices, maybe some pepper and Italian seasoning. Instead of the diced tomatoes, I would add a can of low sodium tomato sauce. I will make this again with those changes. It's the definition of comfort food with not a lot of prep.

I love this recipe! I added sour cream and green onions to my mashed potatoes and swapped red and yellow peppers for the tomatoes and added a bit of better than bullion roast beef to the hamburger but that's it. The base recipe is very delicious and is now a staple in my rotation!

Omitted oil. Fried the onions with the beef. Used a bag of mixed vegetables in place of beans and also added a chopped green pepper. Used 4 large potatoes and added one egg, water, 1 tablespoon butter and a splash of whipping cream when mashing them. This was an easy recipe and made a great casserole. Hubby loved it.
Great recipe, added my own personal twist by sautéing additional vegetables with bacon and to moistened it a bit with beef broth making a gravy...

Very simple and quick recipe! And as other reviews said it is a great base recipe to make your own and add or take away whatever ingredients you decide. I was trying to make something quick since my husband had to go to a meeting so instead of making mashed potatoes from scratch I used a half a bag of frozen mashed potatoes. I also used half a bag of frozen mixed veggies thawed in the microwave instead of fresh green beans. I didn't realize I was out of onions so I used onion powder as a substitute. I also skipped adding the egg to the mashed potatoes but from what I read in the reviews I shouldn't have skipped that. (I will try that the next time I make it!) The last thing I changed was that after I cooked the dish for the 15 minutes I put it under the broiler for a few minutes to get the mashed potatoes a little bit browned. (I skipped the cheddar cheese on top.) My husband and I enjoyed this dish!
Shepherds Pie made with beef is a Cottage Pie. Besides that I substituted peas for the beans.

Never had shepherd's pie before, but have been wanting to try for a long time. This was a great recipe. Even the kids loved it. As I had no canned or frozen veggies on hand, I used some diced yellow and green squash for the vegetables. I doubled the amount of potatoes as I figured two would not be enough. Glad I did! I blended the potatoes with the egg and water and added some pepper and folded the cheese into them as well. Also, after reading reviews, I added garlic salt and brown gravy (from a packet) to the meat mixture. It made it much more flavorful. The only thing I will change in the future would be to not add the egg, as it made the potatoes more fluffy, but turned the dish into mush. I didn't get the desired crust from them. Also, I had to cook for an additional ten minutes and it still did not brown. When I try again without the egg, maybe it will take less time to crust. Great recipe and very versatile!

I cooked the ground beef first & drained it & set aside. Then I cooked the onions and chopped carrots instead of green beans. Added sliced mushrooms after about 10 minutes. After another 10 minutes added the cooked ground beef. Cooked a bit to warm up the beef then put in the casserole dish and topped with mashed potatoes & cheese. I used more cheese than recipe called for. My husband went back for seconds!

My family likes this recipe but I make some changes. I use two pounds of ground turkey. I cook the onion with the turkey, then add in diced tomatoes, 2 cups of thawed mixed veggies (peas, corn, green beans, etc), and a small jar of turkey gravy. Add seasoning as preferred--I often add garlic and Italian seasoning. Put that in the casserole pan and top with 1 packet of instant mashed potatoes, prepared as usual and with an egg added in. Top with cheese and bake.
Used sweet corn and mushrooms in place of string beans and tomato sauce . Then followed the recipe. Did not add any water and glad I didn’t it had enough liquids.
This was so, super simple, and absolutely delicious!!

Wow! The wife went back for thirds. I added green pepper and potabella mushroom to the onions in the pan. Smoked paprika and garlic salt(out of home grown). Dropped the beans and tomatoes but added about 3/4 a can of mixed veges. On top I went with a blend of cheddar, goat mobay, and fresh parmesan.
Outstanding, made it three weeks in a row!

The only thing I did different from the recipe was to season the meat to taste. I think this is great for potluck style gatherings; just double OR triple ingredients depending on gathering size. My husband and I enjoyed it. I will definitely make this again!🥰
I will add more salt and make more mashed potatoes next time. But will definitely make again.
big disappointment! Bland, potatoes had no flavor.
